newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on hedge, commission selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on hedge, commission selling.

text.p: WCE canola ended lower on hedge and commission house selling, traders said.

"There was hedge and commission selling on 90-day storage tickets and technical weakness at the close. There was commercial short covering of the Jan, Cargill was a good buyer of the March," a trader said. Jan-Mar spread at $0.70. January futures crush margin fell to -38.11 from -38.03 Friday on January soyoil, meal. Volume was 3,977 lots with 450 hedges.
Japan bought 3,000-4,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
January canola fell $1.20 to $405.70 and March slipped $0.80 to $406.80. January flax rose $1.50 at $356 on commercial demand.
December feed wheat rose $2 to $170 on commercial demand met by local and hedge selling. Volume was 560 lots.
February western barley fell $0.20 at $138.70 on hedge, local selling with commission and commercials buying at the lows. Volume was 725 lots. Oats and peas did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except peas, oats).
